title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Architecture
description: Understand the open Model Context Protocol specification, JSON-RPC 2.0 transport mechanisms, tools, resources, and prompt templates.

data.text: The Need for a Universal Integration Standard

Before the Model Context Protocol (MCP), every AI ecosystem—OpenAI, Semantic Kernel, LangChain, Claude, Custom enterprise apps—required proprietary connector code to integrate external tools, databases, and APIs. If a company wrote an internal tool for querying sales metrics in PostgreSQL, they had to reimplement it for every individual AI assistant framework. MCP solves this by acting as the 'USB-C for AI applications': an open, vendor-neutral specification allowing any AI client to discover and consume tools and resources from any MCP server.

data.text: MCP Transports: Stdio vs Server-Sent Events (SSE)
MCP specifies two official wire transports powered by JSON-RPC 2.0:

cards.title: stdio (Standard Input/Output)
cards.description: The client launches the MCP server binary as a local child process and exchanges newline-delimited JSON-RPC messages over stdin and stdout. Zero networking overhead, no firewall issues, secure local sandboxing.

cards.title: HTTP with SSE (Server-Sent Events)
cards.description: The client communicates with a remote MCP server over HTTP. The client posts commands to an HTTP endpoint while the server streams asynchronous responses and notifications back via an SSE stream.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: MCP eliminates vendor lock-in by standardizing client-server tool and resource discovery
MCP centers on three primitives: Tools (actions), Resources (context), and Prompts (templates)
Supported transports are stdio (fast local child process) and SSE (remote enterprise HTTP)
All communication is governed by structured JSON-RPC 2.0 message contracts
Adopting MCP enables .NET applications to expose existing enterprise services to any modern AI assistant
data.takeaway: The Model Context Protocol is revolutionizing AI integration. Standardizing on MCP allows .NET developers to build tools and data sources once and use them across any AI tool, assistant, or framework.
